"""Track selection must rank on EVIDENCE (how many track keywords actually hit) and use the
declared track weight only to break an exact tie.

The weight is already a scoring multiplier downstream (run.effective_track_weight feeds
score_opportunity(track_weight=...)). If it also scales the hit count, one declared signal decides
the label AND the score, and a heavy track can take the label away from a track that matched more
of the text. These assert the returned label, never the source text."""
from classify import classify

CFG = {
    "tracks": [
        {"id": "heavy-track", "weight": 1.3, "enabled": True,
         "keywords": ["mcp", "llm", "inference"]},
        {"id": "light-track", "weight": 0.9, "enabled": True,
         "keywords": ["creator", "community", "marketplace", "social"]},
    ],
    "machine_types": ["tool-saas"],
    "focus_topics": [],
    "exclude": [],
}


def test_more_evidence_wins_over_a_heavier_track():
    # 4 light-track hits vs 3 heavy-track hits: the weight must not overturn the evidence.
    out = classify("creator community marketplace for social makers",
                   "an mcp llm inference demo", CFG)
    assert out["track"] == "light-track", out
    assert out["track_matched"] is True, out


# The tie tests deliberately list the LIGHT track first. In the CFG above, heavy-track is first, so
# a tie there is won by heavy-track through declaration order alone and the assertion holds whether
# or not the weight is consulted. That was the original negative control and it was inert: an audit
# hand-applied a repair that deleted the weight from the sort key entirely and it passed 3/3. A
# control that cannot be failed by the wrong repair it was written to reject is not a control.
_TIE_CFG = dict(CFG, tracks=[CFG["tracks"][1], CFG["tracks"][0]])
_TIE_SWAPPED = dict(CFG, tracks=[dict(CFG["tracks"][1], weight=1.3),
                                 dict(CFG["tracks"][0], weight=0.9)])


def test_the_weight_still_breaks_an_exact_tie():
    # NEGATIVE CONTROL for the case above: dropping the weight entirely is not the repair. Three hits
    # each, and the heavier track must win DESPITE being declared second.
    out = classify("mcp llm inference", "creator community marketplace", _TIE_CFG)
    assert out["track"] == "heavy-track", out


def test_swapping_the_two_weights_flips_the_tie_winner():
    # The same control stated as a difference rather than a value, so it cannot be satisfied by any
    # fixed ordering. Identical text, identical declaration order, only the weights exchanged.
    out = classify("mcp llm inference", "creator community marketplace", _TIE_SWAPPED)
    assert out["track"] == "light-track", out


def test_a_lone_hit_in_the_light_track_still_wins_over_nothing():
    out = classify("a creator economy roundup", "", CFG)
    assert out["track"] == "light-track", out
